name: sctp_setopt
prose: Precondition: so is a socket and optval points to a caller-supplied option buffer of optsize bytes for the option optname; p is only passed through to connectx. Postcondition: returns EINVAL if optval is NULL or so->so_pcb is NULL; otherwise it applies the requested socket option (for the slice shown, SCTP_PEER_ADDR_PARAMS updates per-destination, per-association or endpoint-default heartbeat, PMTU, path-max-retrans, DSCP and flowlabel settings, taking and releasing the TCB or INP locks it needs, and SCTP_RTOINFO follows) and returns 0 on success or an errno value (EINVAL, EAFNOSUPPORT, ENOMEM, ENOENT, EPERM, EALREADY, EBUSY, EOPNOTSUPP, ENOPROTOOPT, ENOTSUP or a callee error) depending on the option. For SCTP_PEER_ADDR_PARAMS it returns EINVAL for a nonzero non-wildcard address with no matching net, for conflicting HB_ENABLE/HB_DISABLE or PMTUD_ENABLE/PMTUD_DISABLE flags, for an out-of-range path MTU, and for a no-association request on a non-eligible socket, and EAFNOSUPPORT for an unsupported address family. Any TCB lock obtained by SCTP_FIND_STCB or sctp_findassociation_ep_addr is released before return.
note: The slice is the middle of the big option-setting function sctp_setopt (the old name sctp_sockopt is wrong); contract left empty because the parameters include pointers. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_lower_sosend
prose: Precondition: this is the tail of sctp_lower_sosend, reached with the TCB locked, the association neither about to be freed nor aborted, and `error` holding the result of the data copy or append just before this point. Postcondition: if `error` is nonzero it jumps to the exit. Otherwise, if SCTP_EOF was requested and the whole send was done, it either sends SHUTDOWN, or sets SHUTDOWN_PENDING, or aborts the association with a cause, which sets stcb to NULL and returns ECONNABORTED. It then optionally sends INIT, applies the cwnd and Nagle rules, and under the net epoch runs chunk output, a probe, or control-only output. On exit it releases the create lock if it was taken. If stcb is still non-NULL it undoes the send reservation if local, drops the refcount if applied, and unlocks the TCB. It frees any remaining `top` and `control` mbufs and returns `error`: 0 on success, an errno from earlier steps, or ECONNABORTED.
note: The slice is the tail of sctp_lower_sosend; the name is inferred because the function head is outside the slice, and parameters are pointers so no formal contract. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_arethere_unrecognized_parameters
prose: Precondition: in_initpkt is an mbuf chain holding an INIT or INIT-ACK chunk whose header is cp, param_offset is the offset of its first parameter, abort_processing and nat_friendly are valid pointers, and cookie_found and edmid are valid or NULL. Postcondition: *abort_processing is set to 0 on entry, cookie_found (if non-NULL) is cleared and then set to 1 on a state cookie, edmid (if non-NULL) is set to SCTP_EDMID_NONE and then to the value from a zero-checksum-acceptable parameter, and *nat_friendly is set to 1 on a NAT-support parameter. Each parameter is checked against its size limits. On a bad size (invalid_size path) *abort_processing becomes 1, any earlier error mbuf is freed, and a new protocol-violation cause mbuf holding the offending type and length is returned, or NULL if no parameter header was readable or allocation failed. A hostname parameter sets *abort_processing to 1, frees the earlier error mbuf, and returns an unresolvable-address cause that includes a copy of the parameter, or NULL on allocation or copy failure. An unknown parameter with the 0x4000 bit set has an unrecognized-parameter cause appended to the error mbuf, with padding between entries, or the error mbuf is freed and set to NULL on allocation failure. Unknown parameters with the 0x8000 bit clear stop processing and return the error mbuf built so far, and those with the bit set are skipped. When all parameters are consumed it returns the accumulated error mbuf chain, or NULL if none. The caller owns the returned mbuf chain.
note: Slice is the tail of this function; annotated as the whole function. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output
prose: Precondition: the caller passes a valid mbuf chain m holding the SCTP chunks, a destination sockaddr to, and inp (stcb and net may be NULL; if net is NULL a temporary route is used). Postcondition: this slice covers the AF_INET and the start of the AF_INET6 case. In the AF_INET case, on failure the mbuf chain m is freed and EHOSTUNREACH is returned (no source address, no route, UDP tunneling port 0, or no ro_nh) or ENOMEM (the output header could not be prepended). Otherwise the IP header, optional UDP header and SCTP header are filled in, the checksum is set (zero CRC, software CRC for UDP, or hardware-offload flags), statistics are updated, the packet is passed to SCTP_IP_OUTPUT and its return value is returned (nonzero counts as a send error). A temporary route is freed when net is NULL; otherwise the path MTU is lowered if the route reports a smaller one, or the cached source address is dropped if the route was freed. In the AF_INET6 start, the flow label is chosen and a new header mbuf is prepended to m; if that allocation fails m is freed and ENOMEM is returned.
note: Slice is the middle of a large function; the annotation covers the whole function's visible paths. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_process_cookie_existing
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the TCB lock on stcb and passes a validated COOKIE_ECHO in m with located INIT and INIT-ACK chunks, and writable netp and notification. Postcondition (the part seen here; the function continues past it): in the stream-setup failure branch it unlocks the TCB and returns NULL; in the collision/open branch it stops timers, marks sent chunks for retransmit if the peer tag changed, and if sctp_process_init or sctp_load_addresses_from_init fails it calls sctp_abort_association and returns NULL, otherwise it sets *notification to SCTP_NOTIFY_ASSOC_UP when the state was COOKIE_WAIT or COOKIE_ECHOED, moves the association to OPEN, sends a COOKIE-ACK (plus chunk output if retransmits were marked) and returns stcb with the TCB lock held; in the peer-restart branch with a NAT-capable peer it returns the result of sctp_process_cookie_new, unlocking stcb first if that result is NULL; otherwise it sets *notification to SCTP_NOTIFY_ASSOC_RESTART, resets sequence numbers, mapping arrays and stream state, temporarily drops and retakes the TCB lock (taking the INP-info and INP write locks), frees the queued reset, pending-reply, control, asconf and asconf-ack entries, and sets rcv_edmid from the cookie before continuing beyond this slice.
note: Slice is a middle fragment of sctp_process_cookie_existing; the function continues past the end of the slice, so the final return of the restart path is not visible. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_send_initiate_ack
prose: Precondition: inp is a valid endpoint and the caller holds the inp lock (and the tcb lock if stcb is non-NULL); init_pkt, src, dst, sh and init_chk describe a received INIT chunk. Postcondition: returns nothing; it either sends an ABORT instead of an INIT-ACK (new addresses or a changed encapsulation port in a non-COOKIE_WAIT state, unrecognized parameters requesting an abort, or an unsupported address family), or builds an INIT-ACK with its parameters, addresses, the optional operational error and a signed state cookie in a new mbuf chain and passes it to sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output. It silently returns after freeing the new mbuf chain and op_err on allocation failure, a missing source address, a missing socket, or cookie or padding failure. On a send error it logs it, counts ENOBUFS in the statistics and sets asoc->ifp_had_enobuf (cleared on success); the chain is handed to the output routine and not freed here. In the new-tag case it temporarily drops and retakes the tcb lock, or drops and retakes the inp read lock.
note: The listed name sctp_send_initack is a placeholder; the real function is sctp_send_initiate_ack, and the slice is its tail. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_load_addresses_from_init
prose: Precondition: stcb is a valid association whose TCB lock the caller holds, m is an mbuf chain whose SCTP parameter area starts at offset and ends at limit, and src/dst (and optional altsa) are valid sockaddrs. Postcondition: the source address (altsa if given) and the IPv4/IPv6 addresses listed in the INIT/INIT-ACK parameters are added to stcb->asoc.nets or marked as still present, addresses no longer present are removed and freed, the peer capabilities (ECN, PR-SCTP, auth, asconf, reconfig, idata, NR-SACK, packet-drop, NAT, adaptation, zero-checksum EDMID) are recorded and local features the peer lacks are disabled, the peer HMAC list and chunk list are stored, and the concatenated RANDOM+CHUNKS+HMACS key replaces authinfo.peer_random and the cached keys are cleared, returning 0; it returns a negative code on failure: -1/-2 if adding the source address fails, -3 if the source address belongs to another association (that TCB is unlocked), -4/-7/-10/-12/-16/-19/-21 if the association was freed, -5/-14 for a bad address parameter, -8/-17 if adding an address fails, -13/-22 if an address belongs to another association, -23/-35 for an oversized parameter, -24/-25/-26/-28/-30 if a parameter cannot be read, -27 for a bad RANDOM length, -29 for an invalid HMAC list, -31/-32/-33 for inconsistent auth/asconf support, -34 if key allocation fails, and -100/-101 for a bad SET_PRIMARY parameter. A peer association in COOKIE_WAIT state that holds an address is aborted and the address is then added.
note: Name corrected: the slice is a part of sctp_load_addresses_from_init, not sctp_process_init_ack_parameters. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_handle_sack
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the TCB lock of stcb, the association's sent_queue is ordered by TSN, and m/offset_seg/offset_dup describe the SACK gap-ack and duplicate-TSN blocks that num_seg, num_nr_seg and num_dup count. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; if cum_ack is >= the next TSN to send (send_s), or the biggest gap-acked TSN is >= send_s, it sets *abort_now = 1, aborts the association and returns. If the cum_ack is older than asoc->last_acked_seq it returns without change. If sent_queue, send_queue and stream queues are all empty it only sets peers_rwnd (zeroed below the SWS threshold), clears the retransmit count, stops the send timers, zeroes flight sizes and returns. Otherwise it resets the per-net ack state, marks cum-acked chunks, processes gap and NR-gap segments, stops send timers, sets last_acked_seq = cum_ack and frees all sent_queue chunks with TSN <= cum_ack, wakes the sender, handles revoked chunks and fast-recovery exit, and runs congestion-control updates. It then either completes a shutdown step (aborting with *abort_now = 1 on an incomplete user message in shutdown, or sending SHUTDOWN/SHUTDOWN-ACK and returning) or recomputes peers_rwnd, restarts or stops the send timers, and performs PR-SCTP forward-TSN processing.
note: Placeholder name replaced by the containing function sctp_handle_sack; the slice is only part of it. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output
prose: Precondition: inp is a valid SCTP endpoint, m is an mbuf chain holding the SCTP chunks to send, and either net is a destination or to is a valid destination sockaddr; for the IPv6 branch the destination is AF_INET6. Postcondition: in the IPv6 branch the function builds the IPv6 header (flow label, tos, next header, payload length, source and destination), selects a source address and route, fills in the optional UDP header and the SCTP header, computes the checksum, and calls the IPv6 output routine, which consumes the packet. It then updates statistics and the cached route and source address, and continues with the PMTU check for net. Errors in this part free the mbuf m and return: EINVAL if embedding the scope id fails, EHOSTUNREACH if no source address or route is found or the UDP tunneling port is 0, the error from sa6_recoverscope if recovering the scope fails, and ENOMEM if the output header cannot be prepended. Otherwise it continues past the shown part, so the final return value is not determined by this slice.
note: Slice is the IPv6 branch of sctp_lowlevel_chunk_output; the whole function is annotated, and it has non-integer parameters so no formal contract. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_lower_sosend
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the TCB lock of stcb (with a valid association asoc and socket so), and sndrcvninfo/sinfo_flags describe the send. Postcondition: the function validates the request and returns an errno through its error variable on these paths: EINVAL (SCTP_ADDR_OVER with unknown address or mismatched port, zero-length send without SCTP_EOF, stream number out of range or not open/opening, stream locked to a different stream, last message still being processed), EMSGSIZE (NO_FRAGMENT message above the smallest MTU, or a non-EOR message larger than the send buffer limit), EAGAIN (stream reset in progress), EWOULDBLOCK (non-blocking send with no room), ECONNRESET or ENOTCONN (association aborted or about to be freed while waiting or copying in), EPIPE (association shutting down, the new message is freed), or a socket/block-entry error from sbwait. Otherwise it reserves sndlen bytes in sb_send_resv, may sleep waiting for send-buffer space (dropping and retaking the TCB lock), and then either copies the user data into a new stream queue entry appended to the stream's outqueue with the stream_queue_cnt incremented, or continues the incomplete last message of the stream, setting its processing flag. A zero-length send with SCTP_EOF skips to the EOF handling. This slice ends mid-function, so later steps are not covered here.
note: Slice is the middle of sctp_lower_sosend; annotated as the whole function from the visible part, the tail is not shown. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_lower_sosend
prose: Precondition: the caller passes a valid SCTP endpoint inp (and optionally an existing stcb with its TCB lock held), a destination addr (may be NULL if an association exists), and either uio or an mbuf chain top holding the data. Postcondition: this part resolves or creates the association (an implicit send starts an INIT in COOKIE_WAIT with queue_only set), and fails with errno EINVAL (socket gone, IPv6 address on a non-v6 socket, or abort requested before the association is up), ENOTCONN (address lookup returned a different endpoint, or association about to be freed), ENOENT (no association and no addr, or abort/EOF with no data on a non-existent association), ECONNRESET (association was aborted), EMSGSIZE (abort data too large for an MTU), ENOMEM (no mbuf for the abort cause), or the error from association allocation or cmsg processing; the error paths release the create lock, TCB lock and refcount as appropriate. If SCTP_ABORT is requested on an established association, an abort is sent with an optional user cause, the association is released (stcb set to NULL), and the function ends with error 0 unless an earlier error was set. Otherwise it continues past this section with the TCB locked and the association's refcount held, to the data-queueing code.
note: Function was previously dropped for lack of name in the slice; the slice is the middle of sctp_lower_sosend, so annotate the whole function. [sonnet-5-5]

name: sctp_getsockopt
prose: Precondition: inp is a valid SCTP PCB, optval points to a buffer of at least *optsize bytes, optsize is a valid pointer, and (for the per-association options) the caller holds no lock on the PCB or TCB; this slice covers the cases from SCTP_REUSE_PORT up to SCTP_GET_ASSOC_NUMBER of the option switch, and SCTP_GET_ASSOC_ID_LIST continues past it. Postcondition: for each handled option the value is written into optval and *optsize is set to the size of the option's data; SCTP_CHECK_AND_CAST first rejects a too-small *optsize with an error; error is set to EINVAL for SCTP_REUSE_PORT on a 1-to-many socket, for per-association options with no association and a socket that is not 1-1 (or 1-many with SCTP_FUTURE_ASSOC), for SCTP_CC_OPTION and SCTP_STREAM_SCHEDULER_VALUE without an association, for an out-of-range stream or failing scheduler get-value, for SCTP_GET_ADDR_LEN with an unsupported address family and for SCTP_GET_ASSOC_NUMBER on a 1-1 socket; SCTP_CC_OPTION yields ENOTSUP when the congestion control module has no socket option handler, otherwise the handler's return value; *optsize is left unchanged on those error paths except that it is set after the CC handler is called; a found TCB is unlocked before the case ends and the PCB read lock is released.
note: Fragment of the large option switch inside sctp_getsockopt (named by the enclosing function); annotated as that whole function in summary form. [sonnet-5-5]
